title: The Path to Umiam (Ka Lynti Umiam)
cultural_context: One of the most famous lyrics in Khasi literature celebrating the journey toward the sacred Umiam river, published in 'Ki Jingrwai Khasi' (1960).
lyrics_khasi:
Katba sngi ka dang sah
Ha lyndet Lum Mawpat,
Bad pyrthei ka dang thiab,
Na la ing nga la khlad;
Ba ngan leit sha Umiam,
Ki jat jong nga ki shu lam;
Nga iaid ha ka jingjar-jar,
Khlem da don ba buh kum.

Dohnud jong nga kam tlot,
Nga iohsngew ka jingkhot
Ha ki ksaw shoh lyngngai
Kiba wan na sha rngai,
Kum jingtuid jong ki um
Sha ki them na ki lum;
Nga iohsngew sur batngen,
Kumta nga iaid shaphrang.

Ynda wan ka jingshai
Bad ka miet ka la wai,
Ki lyer step ba pyngngad
Ia syntiew ki pynshad;
Ki sim bneng ruh ba rwai
Sha wahduid ki ia phai;
Ki kynthoh la ki sner
Ban leit sngewbha sa her.

Ka pyrthei kaba khuid,
Ka pyrthei ba laitluid,
Kum kane hangnei ngan shem
La dohnud ban pyndem?
Hangne ksai-kbum ba woh,
Ah! nga sngew la law noh!
La jynjar ba ngan klet,
Shane, pleng, dei ban phet!
lyrics_english:
While the sun still lingered
Behind Mount Mawpat,
And the world was still asleep,
From my home I departed;
To journey toward Umiam,
My footsteps gently led me;
I walked in profound stillness,
With none to question or stay me.

My heart did not falter,
I heard the calling whisper
In sweet enchanting breezes
Arriving from afar,
Like the flowing of clear streams
Toward valleys from high crests;
I heard solace in the notes,
And so I walked onward.

When the morning light dawned
And the dark night receded,
The fresh cool morning breeze
Made every blossom dance;
The celestial birds singing
Turned toward the babbling brook;
Preening their bright feathers
Soaring forth in pure delight.

A world so pure and clean,
A world unchained and free,
Like this where else shall I find
To rest my yearning heart?
Here the tight cords that bound me,
Ah, I feel them all untied!
My sorrows to forget,
Here indeed I must take refuge!
